p.t: In short
Run ads from an **agency account**, not a personal one. A banned personal account is gone for good, and an agency handles support and replacement accounts.
Use **Google Analytics 4 (GA4)** for tracking. The old Universal Analytics is out of use.
Link **Google Analytics only** through the Google and YouTube app. Remove any Google Ads or Merchant Center connection there.
Check your numbers before you scale. Compare cheaper tools first, because **Triple Whale costs $300 per month**.
Give each partner or banner link its own tag, so you can see its visitors and sales in Google Analytics.
Let AI tools gather data and make files. Ask a human expert to read the results.
Facebook's built-in automated rules are rarely worth the effort. Test any paid tool against its monthly cost.
One test found a click fraud app saved no ad money. Compare its savings to its fee in the first month.
Ad accounts, ownership and risk
An **ad account** is the account that pays for and runs your ads.

A personal ad account (opened in your own name) has **no dedicated support**.
If a personal ad account is **banned**, it is gone.

For scaling (raising your ad spend), choose an **agency account**.
The agency handles support and replacement accounts.
The Kuro Network client portal (the provider's website where you manage your account) menu lists: **Ad Accounts**, Request Top-Up, Funds Transfer, Request BM Transfer, Request Unban,

Request BM Verification and Support Chat.
Meta Business Manager (business.facebook.com) is **free**.

Business Manager holds your Facebook page, Instagram page, pixel and audiences.
A pixel is a small tracking code on your store.

Audiences are groups of people you target with ads.
Create audiences under the menu **Audiences**.
Before a holiday promotion starts, you need a **Meta Ads account and a Google Ads account**.
Both accounts need remarketing audiences built. Remarketing means showing ads again to people who already visited your store.
to link Instagram to a Facebook Business account without mixing personal profiles, log in to **Facebook Business Manager > Settings > Assets > Add Instagram Account**.

Select only your business Instagram account.
Microsoft Advertising is Bing's paid ad platform.
Microsoft Advertising needs **its own account**.

Bing Webmaster Tools is a free Bing tool.
Bing Webmaster Tools only reports organic search performance, meaning unpaid search results.

Bing offered a start credit (free ad money for new advertisers) of about **75 to 100 USD**.
Search for the Bing credit offer and sign up through the Microsoft link to claim it.
Google Ads tools and setup
Google Ads management tools include **Keyword Planner** for keyword research (finding the words people search for).
Google Ads management tools include **Google Ads Settings** for setting up campaigns.
Google management tools include **Google Shopping** for product ads that show pictures and prices.
Google management tools include **AdWords Express**, a simplified way to create ads.
The native Google Ads dashboard (the built-in reporting screen) is **free**. It needs no add-on.
Supermetrics is an add-on tool. Treat it as **paid**, and check current pricing before you budget for it.

Start with the native dashboard. Add Supermetrics only when you need one combined sheet across several platforms.
To create a native Google Ads dashboard:

1. **Open** the native Dashboards feature in Google Ads and create a new dashboard. It starts blank.
2. **Add a widget**, for example a chart of conversions by device.

3. **Resize** the widget as needed.
4. **Add more widgets**, such as conversion rate by device, geographic performance by state or a campaign view.
5. **Click Save.**
6. **Return** to the saved dashboard at any time. Check metrics and bid adjustments there, without going through campaigns.
Google Shopping competitor check: open the **Google Analytics** Content report in the left sidebar. Google Analytics is Google's free website statistics tool.

The Content report shows the store pages with the most traffic (visits).
Search those top product pages in **Google Shopping** to see what competitors charge.
Microsoft Advertising (Bing) can import Google Ads campaigns. Importing means copying them over.

Bing does **not** group multiple sellers of the same product in one listing.
So the price comparison that Google shows does not happen on Bing.
Google analytics, GA4 and tracking foundations
Google Analytics is a tracking tool. It shows which pages visitors view.

It shows which pages visitors **leave from**.
It shows how long visitors stay on the website.
Google Analytics 4 (GA4) is the current version of Google Analytics.

GA4 tracks website traffic, conversions (completed goals such as sales), and user behavior.
GA4 can create remarketing audiences.

GA4 **replaced Universal Analytics**.
Universal Analytics (the old version) has been phased out in many accounts. (2023)
Stores should **use GA4**. (2023)
Migration from Universal Analytics to GA4 has its own guided step in the analytics setup. Update your analytics setups to GA4. (2023)
Shopify needs GA4 connected through the **Google channel** (Shopify's link to Google services).

Google removes the old Universal Analytics connection on **July 1**.
Do **not** rely on the old Universal Analytics entry for tracking.

Conversion Pixel App is a Shopify app.
It manages the conversion tracking pixel. A conversion is a completed sale or goal.
The pixel links customer purchases to Google Ads campaigns. This is called attribution: matching a sale to the ad that caused it.

Google and YouTube app is a **free** Shopify app. It connects Google Analytics to your store.
The free plan is **enough** for this purpose.

The app is now owned by Google LLC.
To link Google Analytics to a Shopify store:
1. **Enter the store URL** in the Google Analytics setup. If Google recognizes a Shopify store, it offers Install with Shopify. Click Next to see the instructions.

2. **Search the Shopify App Store for the Google and YouTube app, and choose the free plan**.
3. **Click Install.**
4. After installation, the app appears under **Sales Channels** in the Shopify admin.
Google analytics, GA4 and tracking foundations (continued)
5. In Google Analytics, **copy the Tag ID** of the data stream. A data stream is the flow of visitor data from your store into GA4. The Tag ID is the code that identifies it.
6. In the Google and YouTube app, **follow option one**, the Google Analytics connection that uses the guided Shopify video. Do **not** use option two, because it is more complex.

7. **Paste the Tag ID** where the setup asks for it.
8. **Open the app's Settings and confirm that only one** Google Analytics property is connected.

**Connect neither** Google Ads nor Google Merchant Center through the Google and YouTube app.
That app is meant solely for linking Google Analytics.
If Google Ads or Merchant Center appears as connected under that app's Settings, **remove the connection**.
The person who links Google Analytics through the Google and YouTube app needs **administrator rights** (full access) on that Google Analytics account.
Without administrator rights, the guided connection cannot be completed.
The Google channel setup offers to turn on Google emails and to manage Merchant Center from there. Merchant Center is Google's tool that holds your product list.

Do **not** activate these during the Google Analytics connection.
Set up Merchant Center in its **own later step**.

Use the **feed app's** integration for the Google tracking tag. A feed app sends your product list to Google and other channels. The Google tracking tag is a small code that sends visitor data to Google. (2023)
If tracking fails after moving from Universal Analytics to GA4, contact that app's support through its **help button**, with a screenshot. (2023)

Keep GA4's **default user engagement event settings** when integrating directly with Shopify. (2023)
Changing these settings could affect Shopify analytics. (2023)
Default user engagement events count a visitor after about **10 seconds** on the site. (2023)
The Google Analytics real-time view shows how many people are on the site at a given moment.
Open the real-time view during a **large influencer post** to see the traffic it generates.
Google analytics, GA4 and tracking foundations (continued)
Check traffic platform by platform in Google Analytics. For example, look at Pinterest traffic under **Traffic sources** (the report of where visitors come from). (2022)
Check whether traffic and sales come from that platform **before judging its cost per click** (what you pay each time someone clicks your ad). (2022)
The **Facebook Pixel (Meta's tracking code) should be installed on the store before running paid traffic**. Then analytics data builds up in advance.
Business Manager at business.facebook.com is free to set up. It is where the pixel and analytics are managed.

Meta Pixel Helper is a **browser extension** (a small add-on for your web browser).
Use it to check whether the Meta pixel is installed and firing correctly on a store's pages.

Facebook Pixel Helper is a **free Chrome extension**.
It stays in the top-right area of the browser.
It shows which Facebook Pixel events fire on any website you open. This lets you examine competitor tracking.
Before enabling **Microsoft UET tracking** (Microsoft's Universal Event Tracking code) through the feed app, check the Shopify store for existing conversion tracking or UET scripts.

If you are unsure about an existing script or tag, **contact the app's support first**.
The support link is at the bottom of the setup page, under "Get support".
Facebook Power Editor is a tool for building and editing many ads at once (in bulk).
p.h: Meta Ads: creation, bulk building and testing

p.t: It belongs **after** the audience and message work. That work should be finished first.
AdEspresso or Qwaya (also called Choir) generates **split test** variations. A split test compares versions of an ad against each other.

Variations can cover text, image and color.
They can set up **240 or more variations in about two minutes**.
Use them for split testing, especially when monthly ad spend is around **$2,000 or more**.
Ad manage.ai: media buying automation
Media buying means buying ad space and placements. Ad Manage.ai automates it.

It offers **batch launching** (launching many ads at once).
It integrates with Meta Ads Manager (Meta's native ad screen).

It offers AI-assisted creative generation (AI helps make ad visuals).
It offers cross-platform automation rules (rules that run across several ad platforms).
It integrates with these asset libraries (folders of images and videos): Dropbox, Google Drive, Frame.io, SharePoint, AIR, Focal, Shade, Iconik, Brandfolder, Canva, Figma, YouTube and TikTok.

The platform saves **20-40 hours per month** on media management tasks.
Pricing: a **40% discount on the first month** is available through partnership.

The Essential plan is **recommended for starting**.
The In-House Plus plan offers advanced automation, including cross-platform scaling.
Launch procedure:

1. **Navigate** to the Launcher section and select your ad account.
2. **Click the blue launch button** and select "Select media to use".
3. **Choose a content source**: Dropbox, Google Drive, Frame.io, YouTube, TikTok asset library, or another integration.
4. **Paste a shareable link** or browse folders. Then select specific files or videos to import.
5. **Either add creatives to an existing ad set (if 20 or fewer new ads), or duplicate** an existing ad set and rename it. An ad set is a group of ads with shared settings.
6. **Select the launch status**: Active (starts spending immediately) or Paused (delays the launch).
7. **Load a saved copy template**, or create new copy with primary text, headlines, description, call-to-action and URL parameters, including UTM tracking.

A call-to-action is the button text, and UTM tracking is a tag added to a link to show where a click came from.
8. **Review all settings** and click "Launch Ads".

9. **Wait about one minute** for the launch to complete.
Ads launch in about **one minute on average** in Ad Manage.ai.
Ad manage.ai: media buying automation (continued)
Meta's native Ads Manager takes longer, with more sequential steps and upload times.

Click **Edit in Table Mode** to assign different settings to individual ads in the same batch launch.
Card view applies identical settings to all ads.
Table Mode lets you customize targeting, budget or other fields per ad.
The **Existing Ads tab** in Media Library shows all ads in your connected Meta ad account. They can be active, paused or inactive.
Use it to see total spend, ad count and launch status. This helps you avoid duplicate creatives and track performance.

When you duplicate an ad set, a "Copy ads to new ad set" checkbox appears.
Leave it **unchecked** if you only want to copy the ad set structure and settings.
**Check it** only if you also want to copy the original ads into the new ad set.
After launching, click **"View in Meta"** or "View Launch" to open that ad directly in Meta's native Ads Manager.
Ad Manage.ai includes a **free Google Sheets plugin** for bulk ad launches.
Connect your spreadsheet to trigger automatic ad launches from Sheets, without using the platform interface.

The Inspiration tab's Clone Ad feature runs on a **1,000-credit monthly cycle**. Credits are the units the feature uses.
Each cloned ad uses credits.
When credits run out, the feature is unavailable until the cycle resets. The cycle resets **every 3 days**.
API reports (data pulled automatically from Meta) take **20-30 minutes** to refresh with current data from Meta.
While loading, the platform shows the most recent available data for Top Creatives, Fatigued Ads, Landing Pages and custom reports.
TikTok Ads

TikTok pixel setup: in TikTok Ads Manager, go to **Tools > Events > Manage Web Events**.
Then click **Create Pixel > Partner Setup > Next > Shopify**.

Set **Data Sharing for the pixel to Maximum**.
TikTok Pixel Helper is a Shopify app. It connects the TikTok pixel to a Shopify store.

A new TikTok Ads account is under review after setup.
Activation can take **up to 24 hours**. Campaigns can run only after that.
The account is active once **TikTok Marketing shows as Active**.
TikTok Ads Manager is used to run Spark Ads (TikTok ads built from existing posts) through a generated authorization code, or to upload traditional ads.
Use a **separate Ads Manager with its own email** for paid work.
TikTok UTM procedure, to track ads after iOS tracking limits (Apple restrictions that block some tracking). A UTM is a tag added to a link:

1. **Open a UTM builder** for TikTok, for example the one offered by PP Ads. A builder is a tool that creates tracking links.
2. **Paste the product page URL** into the builder.

3. **Copy the generated URL.**
4. **Paste the generated URL** into the website URL field of the TikTok ad.
The UTM parameters pass campaign, ad group and ad names to Shopify. This lets you track ads after iOS tracking limits.
Pinterest performs **better in some niches** than others. (2024)
p.h: Pinterest ads: account, profile and verification

p.t: It is worth connecting when the store already gets Pinterest traffic, or when it fits the marketing plan. (2024)

Connecting it through Shopify is simple and carries **little cost**. (2024)
So there is rarely a reason **not to try**. (2024)

Pinterest can be connected to a store.
small-budget Pinterest ads can be tested.
Pinterest business account setup, option A:

1. **Either convert a normal Pinterest account to a business account via Settings, or go directly** to ads.pinterest.com.
2. **Fill in** the basic business details.

3. **Wait** until the account shows as ready.
Pinterest business account setup, option B (full checklist):
1. **Either convert your personal account to a business account in the account settings, or create** a new account at ads.pinterest.com.

2. **Enter the profile name** as your store name. For a general store, use the general store name.
3. **Enter your website link.**

4. **Select a country**: your home country or the US. Pinterest allows targeting any country.
5. **Select the brand focus.** If unsure, choose Other or Home.
Pinterest ads: account, profile and verification (continued)

6. **Select up to three options** from the focus list, such as "sell more products".
7. **Describe the business as online retail or marketplace, and select Shopify** as the platform.

8. **Answer yes** to being interested in advertising.
9. **Enter your phone number** if you want to use Pinterest support, or skip it.
Account setup details: fill in the store name, website, and country. Your own country is fine. There is no need to choose the United States only.

Choose brand focus: the top three options, for example "sell more products".
Choose business type "Online retail or marketplace", with Shopify selected.

Answer **yes** to being interested in advertising.
Check the business account. The profile should show the label **"Business"**.

The menu should show an **"Ads" section**.
Profile > Settings is where these details are verified.

Business profile checklist: a business account shows **"Business"** on the profile.
It also shows an **"Ads" section**.
Profile preparation procedure:

1. **Change the username** to match the brand or product.
2. **Change the profile image.**
3. **Add a short About Us section.**
4. **Add a cover image.**
5. **Claim the website (prove you own the domain) by adding a TXT record** to the domain DNS, or by adding the HTML tag. A TXT record is a text entry in your domain settings.

DNS is the system that points your domain name to your site.
Profile detail: set the username to the store name (or product name).

Upload the store or brand logo as the profile image.
Write a short "about" section of about **five to six lines**. This can be generated with ChatGPT.

Add a cover image, such as a store banner.
A phone number is **optional**. It is not used for verification.
Add it only if you want access to Pinterest support for banned accounts or ad insights.

Do **not rely** on their guidance. Their agents are not focused on direct response marketing (ads that ask people to act now).
Website verification (HTML tag option):

1. In Pinterest settings, go to **Claimed account**, then **Claim website**, and choose the **HTML tag** option.
2. **Copy the meta tag.**
3. **Paste it into the Shopify theme file theme.liquid (the main page template of your theme), just below the canonical URL line** (the line naming the page's official address). Then save.
4. **Return to Pinterest**, click Continue, enter the store name and click **Verify**.
Pinterest ads: Shopify connection, payment and conversions
Install the Pinterest app in Shopify:

1. In Shopify, go to **Apps**, then **App settings**, then the Shopify App Store.
2. **Search for Pinterest** and install the Pinterest app.
3. **Connect your Pinterest account** through the sales channel. A sales channel is a place where you sell, such as Pinterest.

4. Go to the **Marketing section and confirm that the Pinterest tag is installed**. This is the key step for tracking.
5. **Continue the setup** in the app and proceed to billing.

Pinterest setup in Shopify, in order:
1. **Install the Pinterest app** from the Shopify App Store, and connect the Pinterest account.
2. **Add the Sales channel.**

3. Go to the **Marketing section and confirm the Pinterest tag is installed**. This is the key step for tracking.
4. **Click continuous setup.**

5. **Go to ads, then billing**, and enter business details.
6. **Add a payment method**: a credit or debit card, or a **virtual card** (a card number made for online payments).

7. **PayPal is not accepted.**
Pinterest does **not allow listing a product without merchant approval**. Merchant approval is Pinterest's review that lets products be listed for sale.

Merchant approval is a non-essential extra.
Rejections often come from **weak product descriptions**.
So a rejected shopping merchant account should **not stop the ad setup**.
Shopping merchant approval can stay pending or be rejected, often because of product description issues.

This blocks product listings, but it is **not required** to run Pinterest ads.
So it is **not a reason to stop**.

Enabling conversion campaigns when the error "increase your conversion events" appears:
1. **Open a product page** of the store.
2. **Open the browser developer tools** (built-in tools that show page code). Right-click > Inspect, or More tools > Developer tools if inspect is disabled.
3. **Go to the Console** (the part of developer tools where you run code).
4. **Paste the provided conversion-trigger code (the code is not shown here) and run it 10 to 20 times**.
5. **Wait 5 to 10 minutes** until the conversion event is active and the conversion campaign option appears.
Microsoft Ads (Bing)

Microsoft Ads can **import Google Ads campaigns**. (2021)
Make changes in **Google Ads first**, where most data and sales are. (2021)

Sync to Microsoft once a batch of changes is approved. (2021)
Syncing means copying changes over. You can optionally sync only new updates. (2021)

Import procedure (2025):
1. **Import your Google Ads campaigns** into Microsoft Ads.
2. **Immediately lower the budgets** of the imported campaigns. Imports carry over the Google budgets.

3. For example, a **$20 per day Google budget should be reduced to $5 per day** in Microsoft.
4. **Scale the Microsoft budgets gradually** over time.
Dynamic retargeting shows ads that automatically display the products each visitor viewed.

ROI Hunter is a Shopify app that sets up dynamic retargeting **without coding**.
Search for the **exact name "ROI Hunter"** in the Shopify App Store.

A generic search for Shopify dynamic retargeting returns other apps.
ROI Hunter is a **free Shopify app**.
Dynamic retargeting on the Google Display Network (Google's network of sites and apps that show ads) can be set up **without paying** for a separate developer or code work.

Installing it and syncing it with the store is all that is needed to create the audiences and campaigns.
Do **not manage ROI Hunter campaigns from inside Shopify**.

Make all campaign and budget changes **directly in Google Ads**.
The Shopify side is only for setup and sync.
Dropship Toolkit is a website with a break-even ROAS calculator for dropshipping stores.
ROAS means return on ad spend: sales divided by ad spend. Break-even ROAS is the point where you neither make nor lose money.
Enter the **selling price**, the **cost of goods (what you pay the supplier) and the fulfillment cost** (packing and shipping).
The result is the break-even ROAS. Use it **before setting scaling thresholds** (the numbers at which you raise spend).
Use it **before running ads** to check whether a product can be profitable at a given price.
Attribution and profit tracking
Conflict note: sources disagree on when to adopt Triple Whale.
One source says to use it for early-stage testing when accuracy matters for budget decisions.
Two others say to consider it only once the store is consistently profitable and to compare it with a cheaper option first. Apply the first when verifying metrics before scaling.

Apply the second when deciding whether to pay for a tool.
**Triple Whale**
Cost: $300/month
Accuracy (as stated): 80% for sales, ROAS and ad performance

Use when: Early-stage testing and verifying metrics before scaling; or, once the store is consistently profitable
Source ids: ,,,
**Northbeam**

Cost: $900/month
Accuracy (as stated): 100%
Use when: Only if the business generates enough profit margin to justify the cost

**Cometly**
Cost: Not stated
Accuracy (as stated): Not reliable
Use when: Do not use

**Converge**
Cost: Possibly lower than Triple Whale
Accuracy (as stated): Not stated

Use when: Compare with Triple Whale before paying
**Free UTM tracking app**
Cost: Free option

Accuracy (as stated): Not stated; UTM data is not perfect either
Use when: Cross-check Facebook data against actual sales
Attribution means matching each sale to the ad that caused it.
Triple Whale is attribution software. It captures precise ad performance metrics (numbers) when you analyze and improve your creatives (ad visuals and text).

Triple Whale is a tracking and analytics platform that costs **$300/month**.
It is **80% accurate** in measuring sales, ROAS and ad performance.
Use it to **verify your metrics before scaling ads**, because inaccurate tracking wastes budget.

Triple Whale is used to track sales and ROAS for winning products.
It replaces manual tracking of other ad metrics once a product is clearly profitable.

Cometly is a tracking platform that does **not work reliably** and wastes money.
**Do not use it.** Choose Triple Whale or Northbeam instead.
Attribution and profit tracking (continued)
Northbeam is a tracking platform that costs **$900/month and gives 100% accuracy**.
Use it **only if your business generates sufficient profit margin** (money left after costs) to justify the cost.
Otherwise, use Triple Whale ($300/month, 80% accuracy) for early-stage testing.
Triple Whale is a paid attribution tool. It reconciles sales that Facebook reports with real orders.

Cheaper alternatives such as Converge exist, at possibly lower prices.
Because the tool costs money, consider it **only once the store is consistently profitable**.

**Compare it with a cheaper option first.**
A UTM tracking app with a **free option** can cross-check Facebook data against actual sales.
UTM data is not perfect either, but it is a useful second source.
A paid attribution tool such as Triple Whale is worth considering once the store is consistently profitable. Cheaper alternatives exist.

True Profit shows **profit per campaign**.
Its highest plan can be used, reported at about **$150 per month**.
It helps make more calculated scaling decisions, but it is **not essential at the beginning**.

The Conversios GA4 app connects Google Analytics 4 and supports Google SEO tracking.
It is **needed when scaling**, not at the foundation stage.
Microsoft Clarity is an additional analytics tool. It is shown in Customer events (Shopify's list of tracked visitor actions).
Unique coupons, dedicated phone numbers or separate addresses for each ad let you trace **every response to its source**.
Use them to compare headlines, publications and offers on a **cost-per-customer** basis (what you pay to win one customer).

Telephone response lines are more convenient for many people than mailing a coupon.
They can be measured as a **separate response channel**.
Include a phone option in offers, and **track it separately**.
UTM tracking for partners and banners
A UTM is a tag added to the end of a link.

It tells Google Analytics (a free Google tool that counts visitors and sales) where a visitor came from.
To add a partner or banner link with UTM tracking:

1. Choose the destination URL (the web address the link opens).
2. Open a UTM builder (a tool that makes tagged links).
**Set utm_source to banner ad**, utm_medium to banner, and utm_campaign to the partner URL. utm_source is where the visitor came from. utm_medium is the type of channel. utm_campaign is the campaign

name.
4. Leave the **campaign ID** empty. The campaign ID is a code number for the campaign. You do not need it here.

5. Copy the generated link (the finished tagged link) and send it to the partner.
6. **Check** the traffic (number of visitors), country and sales of that source in Google Analytics.
**Supermetrics** is a Google Sheets add-on.
An add-on is an extra tool that plugs into Google Sheets (a free online spreadsheet).
Supermetrics connects to ad accounts (the accounts where your ads run) such as Google Ads, Bing Ads and Facebook Ads. **It pulls their data into a sheet.**
The data lands in a regular spreadsheet. So you can use Google Sheets formulas (ready-made calculations) and conditional formatting (rules that color cells automatically) on it directly.
**Manus** is an AI agent (an AI tool that carries out tasks on its own).
Manus can connect to a Meta ad account (the ad account for Facebook and Instagram ads) through Meta marketing tools.
Manus reads the ad-level names (the name of each single ad) and builds a report.
Manus **uses Python code** (a programming language) to process the exported data (data saved from the ad account) and produce the final file.

**Manus** is an AI agent that can connect to a Meta ad account.
Before pulling data, Manus can load a Meta Ads analysis skill (a ready-made set of instructions for the AI).
When this was written, Meta (Facebook) had just acquired Manus. **Its plans and features may change.**
Reporting and AI reporting limits (continued)

Setting up an AI creative-count report in Manus (a creative is one ad design):
1. **Go to Manus and connect the Meta ad account.**
2. Send a prompt (a written instruction to the AI) that names the ad account, describes the report and attaches an example report.
3. State what to leave out: iterations (small changes to an existing ad) and new concepts (brand-new ad ideas).
4. State which field to group by: product type, taken from the ad naming convention (the fixed way your ads are named).

5. **Review the delivered report**, which can be produced as a spreadsheet.
Prompt for the creative-count report (use as written, replacing the bracketed placeholders):
I need you to look at the ad account [AD ACCOUNT LINK]. I need a report like the attached example that tracks the total number of creatives launched per month per product.
Now note that we do not track iterations or new concepts.
What I need is the report by product type, which is part of our naming convention at the ad level (for example: Mixed, Oodie, Weighted Blanket, [OTHER PRODUCT TYPES]).
Count each ad once in the month it launched, show the monthly totals per product type, and deliver the final report as a spreadsheet.
When you ask an AI agent for an ad account report, **attach a screenshot or recording of an example report**.

Or describe the output in exact words. In your words, state what must be counted.
In your words, also state what must be excluded (for example iterations or new concepts).

In your words, also state which naming field to group by.
Conflict note (the sources disagree): Manus can connect to a Meta account and build reports from it.

**Current AI reporting tools such as Manus are not yet reliable** for interpreting ad account results.
**Use the AI for data gathering and file production.**
**Use human analysis** from mentors, group calls or one-on-one coaches to interpret the data.
In Excel (Microsoft's spreadsheet program), the status bar (the thin bar at the bottom of the window) **shows Average, Count and Sum** for a selected range of cells (a group of selected cells).
Example: selecting 5 values that sum to 273 gives an average of 54.6.
Automation Limits
Conflict note (the sources disagree): **Ad Manage.ai** offers cross-platform automation rules. Cross-platform means across several ad platforms.
An automation rule is a setting that changes ads on its own.
Older advice (2020) says **automating ads with tools like Zapier is not recommended**. Zapier is a tool that connects apps and runs tasks between them automatically.

Facebook's built-in automated rules (Facebook's own settings that act on ads automatically) are occasionally useful.
**They are rarely worth the effort.**
Preflect AI is an ad automation tool. It runs campaigns across Facebook, Google and TikTok. A campaign is a set of ads with one goal.

Preflect AI costs **about $500 per month**.
Preflect AI has **no minimum ad spend** (no required minimum budget for ads).

It suits owners who want a hands-off setup (little work from you).
But **someone still has to read the data** and decide the next test.

Click fraud means fake clicks on your ads that you still pay for.
**a separate click fraud app is not necessary.**
Instead, monitor all ad campaigns.
Then **exclude** Google Display Network sites (websites where Google shows banner ads) that bring in little value or show poor results. Exclude means block your ads from showing there.

one operator (one seller) tested a click-fraud protection app for one month.
The app **did not save any ad money**, so it was not recommended.
**Compare any savings against the monthly fee within the first month** before keeping such a tool.
